body.heading: Why most apologies miss
paragraphs: 'Sorry if you were offended' apologises for the other person's feelings. 'Sorry, but I was tired' hands the fault straight back. Both protect the apologiser more than they repair anything, and listeners can tell instantly.
A landing apology does three things: it names the specific thing, it owns it without decoration, and it acknowledges the effect it had.

body.heading: The three-part shape
paragraphs: Try: 'I interrupted you three times in that meeting. That was dismissive, and it must have been frustrating in front of everyone. I'm sorry.' Specific, owned, aware of impact — nothing else required.
Then comes the hardest part: stop talking. Let the other person respond however they respond. An apology is an offering, not a transaction, and forgiveness is theirs to time.

description: A real apology is a small craft: name it, own it, skip the excuses — and it can change the weather of a whole relationship.
